claims.evidence: In the provided photos, I can see Nikon branding and a DSLR with a lens, but I cannot read 'D750' or any model identifier clearly.
Photos show boxed/packed items; there is no close-up of the sensor, body wear, buttons, or mount to confirm condition.
No powered-on test, no screen-on photo, no shutter actuation, no menu/AF confirmation.
No shutter count screenshot or camera screen showing shutter count.

claims.claim: no fungus or scratch on the lens
claims.evidence: Lens front glass is not shown in a way that lets me confirm fungus/scratches; no close-up of lens elements.

claims.claim: Original battery and charger, never repaired
claims.evidence: No photo of the battery/charger labels or any repair/servicing documentation.

risks.risk: Model mismatch (could be another Nikon DSLR; seller says D750 but photos don’t show the model clearly).
risks.proof: Ask for a photo of the camera with the model name visible (e.g., 'D750' on the body) and/or the EXIF/firmware screen showing model.
risks.if_unproven: Price as a generic used Nikon DSLR body (worst case: not confirmed as D750).

risks.risk: Not actually working / hidden faults (shutter, mirror, AF, buttons, sensor).
risks.proof: Ask for a short video: power on, menu navigation, autofocus on a target, and a live view shot + one shutter click.
risks.if_unproven: Price as not guaranteed working (worst case: needs service).

risks.risk: Lens condition unknown (fungus, haze, scratches, separation).
risks.proof: Ask for close-up photos of the lens front element and rear element (through the mount), taken in bright light at angles to reveal scratches/fungus.
risks.if_unproven: Price as lens may have issues (worst case: treat as needing cleaning/possible defects).

risks.risk: Shutter count claim not verifiable; could be much higher.
risks.proof: Ask for a screenshot/photo from a shutter-count tool or the camera info screen showing shutter count.
risks.if_unproven: Price as higher shutter wear (worst case: not under 5,000).

risks.risk: Body-only vs kit confusion (photos show a lens mounted; seller claims 'Body').
risks.proof: Ask for a photo showing exactly what is included laid out (body, lens if any, battery, charger) with a checklist.
risks.if_unproven: Price as body-only if that’s what you’re buying (worst case: lens not included).

proof_requests: A clear photo of the camera body showing the exact model text 'D750' (or a screen showing model/firmware).
A screenshot/photo of shutter count (from a shutter-count tool) showing the number.
A short powered-on video: menu on screen, autofocus working, and one shutter actuation.
Close-up lens photos: front element and rear element (through the mount) in bright light to check fungus/scratches.
Photos of included items laid out: battery label, charger label, and confirmation whether lens is included or not.
response.reason: The photos confirm Nikon-branded packaging and a DSLR setup, but they do not clearly show the exact model (D750) or any verifiable proof of shutter count, working status, or lens condition—so a worst-case price cannot be set confidently from the provided evidence.
